title: Move wiretap error report routines to libwiretap

notes.body: I seem to have introduced some unintended whitespace changes, I will fix that.
If the capture file routines are moved to libwiretap, perhaps moving failure_message to libwsutil makes sense?

added 3 commits
  • af7b8dfd - EditorConfig: Fix setting to match modeline and indentation
  • 41f5eeaa - wiretap: Make error reporting more usable as stand-alone library
  • 21251599 - Remove capture file routines from wsutil
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18164/diffs?diff_id=1188227117&start_sha=1471523f485fd112e72fb4b2b9661956a77b0d1c)

It shouldn't all go into wsutil including the `cfile_*` routines but splitting half and half between wsutil and wiretap would probably make sense.

But I was hoping to leave that as future work. :slight_smile:

I did not read all of #20108 but this is my understanding of that issue and the fix by @johnthacker :

>>>
This also removes an indirect dependency of wsutil on libui,
which should not be a problem for programs linking with libui.
    
However not all programs do, such as dumpcap.
    
Dumpcap needs to call init_report_message() or it might crash,
this was fixed with a workaround in commit
a72f13513e99796d230e8a32d3b2520907e1f51f, which is now unnecessary.
    
The failure message routines that do not use a cfile parameter
could probably be moved to wsutil and reused in dumpcap to
avoid copy pasting the printf callbacks.
>>>

Several of the routines in alert_box.c are unused after doing this. Does this change the pop up alert boxes in any way for when merging and text import is done within the GUI? It's changing from having specific alert box routines that both generate text and the pop-up to generating the same failure text for both GUI and text mode, and then displaying the text using the standard failure alert box, as I read it.
I think you are right. The `cfile_*` routines probably need to call `report_failure()` instead. Good catch, thanks. I will test it later.

I just noticed there is a `wtap_strerror()` too. I think using that it is reasonable for a wiretap user to implement error messages without relying on `cfile_*`, which was the original motivation for this change.

Yeah I think I'll stick to using `wtap_strerror()` + err_info when necessary. These function seems to be sugar to use application friendly names and such, which is appropriate for libui. Sorry for the noise.
I agree with the comment in the source though, still would be nice to remove the cfile routines from `wsutil/report_msg.h`, or at least allow them to be NULL.

commits_data.title: Remove capture file routines from wsutil
commits_data.message:
Remove capture file routines from wsutil

wsutil users need not have any concept of a capture file,
and so should not be required to implement a report routine
for such.

This also removes an indirect dependency of wsutil on libui,
which should not be a problem for programs linking with libui.

However not all programs do, such as dumpcap.

Dumpcap needs to call init_report_message() or it might crash,
this was fixed with a workaround in commit
a72f13513e99796d230e8a32d3b2520907e1f51f, which is now unnecessary.

The failure message routines that do not use a cfile parameter
could probably be moved to wsutil and reused in dumpcap to
avoid copy pasting the printf callbacks.

commits_data.title: wiretap: Make error reporting more usable as stand-alone library
commits_data.message:
wiretap: Make error reporting more usable as stand-alone library

libwiretap users would benefit from good textual error messages for various
wiretap error codes but for that they are forced to link with "libui",
or copy the failure_message.c source code somewhere, and depend on
an indirect error printing callback chain.

Fix that by moving the error message generating code to libwiretap.
